articles.title: 'He was swinging it both ways': How Jasprit Bumrah kept New Zealand batters guessing
articles.summary: Henry Nicholls had a tough time facing Jasprit Bumrah on the opening day of the first Test against India in Wellington on Thursday.
articles.body: Henry Nicholls had a tough time facing Jasprit Bumrah on the opening day of the first Test against India in Wellington on Thursday. The New Zealand batter said Bumrah's ability to swing the ball both ways kept the batters under pressure.Bumrah troubled the New Zealand batters with his movement through the air and his unusual bowling action. He picked up three wickets as the hosts struggled at 70/5 before Nicholls and Glenn Phillips led a strong recovery.Nicholls remained unbeaten on 113 as New Zealand finished the day at 243/5. Speaking after the day's play, he praised Bumrah's bowling and said facing him was a big challenge."Bumrah was swinging it both ways and putting guys under some serious pressure. It's a great challenge," said Nicholls.'He's certainly an incredible bowler': Nicholls on BumrahNicholls has faced Bumrah several times in the past. He felt that knowing the Indian pacer's unusual action helped him to some extent, but admitted that Bumrah remained difficult to face."He's obviously got a unique action and, lucky enough, I've played him a few times and that gives you a little bit of a benefit. But he's certainly an incredible bowler in all formats," he said.The left-hander was particularly impressed with the way Bumrah moved the ball in both directions."Today, the way he was swinging the ball both ways was incredible bowling. I'm sure tomorrow morning it'll be more of the same and another tough challenge," he added.India's bowlers put New Zealand under pressure in the first session and picked up five wickets. Nicholls acknowledged the quality of the Indian attack and the questions they asked the hosts."They asked fantastic questions, certainly in that first session. You saw that from the pressure we were under," he said.'The way he counter-attacked made it easier for me': Nicholls on PhillipsNew Zealand were in trouble at 70/5 when Nicholls found support from Glenn Phillips. The two put together an unbeaten 173-run stand for the sixth wicket to bring their team back into the game. Phillips was unbeaten on 94 at stumps.Nicholls said Phillips' attacking approach helped him settle at the other end."That partnership and the way Glenn played really alleviated my role. The way he counter-attacked certainly made it a bit easier for me," he said.He also praised Phillips for his aggressive batting and quick running between the wickets."He's great. The way he counter-attacks and the way he runs between the wickets as well, I think we gel quite well in that respect. We're both very busy," Nicholls said.'As many as we can get': Nicholls on New Zealand's targetNicholls said batters need to be patient against a strong bowling attack like India's and wait for opportunities to score runs."If they're going to bowl good balls, live with that, control what we can control and be able to score from there," he said.With New Zealand recovering from a difficult position, Nicholls said the focus would be on building on the partnership and adding as many runs as possible on the second day."As many as we can get, to be honest. It's obviously nice that Glenn and I are in overnight. For us, it's about getting on with doing the hard work again."Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Jasprit Bumrah and the rest: The familiar storyline replays at Basin Reserve
articles.summary: WELLINGTON: Minutes after Devdutt Padikkal dropped a regulation catch off centurion Henry Nicholls, Rishabh Pant, with his hands behind his back, stared
articles.body: WELLINGTON: Minutes after Devdutt Padikkal dropped a regulation catch off centurion Henry Nicholls, Rishabh Pant, with his hands behind his back, stared at the replay on the giant screen. Pant was distraught after losing the opportunity to break the Nicholls-Glenn Phillips partnership, summing up India's day. The body language became flatter, and the players dragged themselves around the field, waiting for the umpires to call it a day.The unbeaten 173-run stand allowed the hosts to stage an emphatic fightback and exposed vulnerabilities in India's inexperienced bowling attack. Jasprit Bumrah was relentless from one end, but containing the batters became difficult after the pitch lost its initial spice and the moisture evaporated under the harsh sun. There was a light shower before the Indian team arrived at the venue, but Wild Welly was on snooze mode as conditions remained very pleasant after that.There were no gusts of wind or dark grey clouds, and while India did come hard with the new ball, they allowed the advantage to slip away with some lacklustre bowling in the post-lunch session. Bumrah, on either side of the break, set the game up nicely but didn't get support from the other end.The ghosts of the Manchester Test were back haunting Anshul Kamboj as the Haryana fast bowler lost his zip and speed as the game progressed. Akash Deep was impressive but didn't get the rub of the green as he bowled much better than the figures suggest.The biggest letdown of the day was Prasidh Krishna's manner of operation. India are obsessed with tall fast bowlers who can hit the deck hard, but Prasidh lacked penetration and control during his 16-over spell. Plenty of comfortable half-trackers were dispatched with disdain, continuing the familiar storyline of Bumrah and the rest at the Basin Reserve.Playing his first Test since the home Test against South Africa last year, Bumrah was on the money from the word go. It took the bowler just three deliveries to draw first blood, and he was very sharp, beating both edges of the batters. There was encouraging seam movement for the bowler, and he rarely missed his mark, consistently finding the ideal good-length spot.His seven-over spell, two before lunch and five after, was in unplayable territory as he asked many questions. The set-up for Darryl Mitchell, which included a short-leg fielder and consistently targeted the stumps, worked because the right-hander kept walking towards the deliveries to negate the movement. Result: Bat-pad to Yashasvi Jaiswal, who took a sharp catch.Tom Blundell came in against an on-song Bumrah and survived only 22 deliveries before nicking one to Shubman Gill. At 70/5, India were one wicket away from entering the New Zealand lower order, but the moment never arrived. For the next 322 deliveries, Gill changed his bowlers, swapped their ends, even took the new ball when it became available close to stumps, but nothing worked.There was no option but to bowl spin from one end to keep the over-rate in check, which further allowed the Nicholls-Phillips stand to grow in confidence and flourish. When they return to the field on Day 2 of the Test, India would hope they can replicate the morning session from the opening day and will again pin their hopes on that man Bumrah.Brief ScoresNew Zealand: 243 for 5 after 83 overs (Henry Nicholls 113 not out, Glenn Philips 94; Jasprit Bumrah 3/52)Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Venugopal Rao: 'Built a cricket ecosystem from scratch, now ready for the next chapter'
articles.summary: BENGALURU: Former India cricketer Venugopal Rao says he is \"happy\" and \"content\" when asked what's next for him after ending his four-and-a-half-year
articles.body: BENGALURU: Former India cricketer Venugopal Rao says he is "happy" and "content" when asked what's next for him after ending his four-and-a-half-year association with GMR Group's cricket franchises, where he served as Director of Cricket."I am in Hyderabad, enjoying my time away from cricket. Now I'm taking some time out to be with my family. My kids have also been asking for my time, so that's important," Rao tells TimesofIndia.com.The 44-year-old has been the architect of the GMR Group's cricketing operations across the globe. He played a pivotal role in guiding Dubai Capitals to the ILT20 title in 2025 and was appointed Delhi Capitals' Director of Cricket for the 2025 and 2026 IPL seasons. He also joined Seattle Orcas as General Manager of Cricket Operations and has helped steady the ship at Southern Brave in The Hundred, a franchise in which the GMR Group has invested heavily."For four-and-a-half years, I was involved day in and day out, setting up the entire system. When I came in, nothing was in place. I built the whole cricket ecosystem, brought people in, and they did well," he says."But I will definitely get involved with teams and do something in cricket again. I can't keep myself away from the game for too long. For the next four or five months, I'll take some time and see what happens. I'm looking forward to opportunities and will see where things go," adds Rao, a veteran of 121 first-class matches.Under Venugopal Rao and head coach Hemang Badani, the Delhi-based franchise finished fifth and sixth in IPL 2025 and 2026, respectively. Sourav Ganguly has now been appointed as Delhi Capitals' head coach ahead of IPL 2027. The move follows the agreement reached between DC co-owners GMR Sports India Pvt Ltd and JSW Sports, under which the two partners would alternate control of the franchise's operations in two-year cycles.“When you look back at our first season (IPL 2025), especially the two games against Mumbai Indians, one at home and one away, I think we could have won both. In the first game in Delhi, we had four or five run-outs, which cost us the match. Karun played a superb knock, and we could have chased the target comfortably. Even in the Mumbai game, we had four or five run-outs, which again cost us," Rao reflects."In the Mumbai game, Axar Patel missed out due to illness. If you look at the surface, it was turning, and Mitchell Santner was a crucial bowler for them who picked up an important wicket. Axar was a big miss for us, not just with the ball but also while batting. As a left-hander, he would have been better equipped to tackle left-arm spin."Those were the two games in our first season that we missed out on, and winning them could have helped us qualify for the knockouts."Rao feels that even in the second season, in 2026, they were in contention for the playoff spots and could have qualified with a bit of luck."Even in the second season, if you look back at the home game against Gujarat Titans, David Miller was on strike. We needed two runs off two balls, but we couldn't win the game. That was our biggest disappointment. A player like Miller should have finished that game," he says."There was also the game against Punjab in which we scored 265. A lot of people say we should have defended that total, but if you look at the circumstances, Lungi Ngidi got injured and had to go to the hospital. That cost us around four hours. At the same time, we dropped eight catches."Normally, if you score 265 and drop eight catches, it's difficult to defend that total. If we had won those two games, Gujarat would have finished in the top two. That's how the IPL works, and we had to accept it," he adds.On the debate over whether Axar Patel or KL Rahul should lead Delhi Capitals (DC), Rao believes the incoming leadership should be allowed to operate without interference.“Whoever takes over should be given a free hand. Whether it’s Axar or KL, both have played at this level and understand the game. I have always believed in giving people freedom. Mistakes can happen, but your intentions should be good. If they are, you should have the clarity and freedom to take decisions," he says.Rao cites KL Rahul's turnaround as an example. After a slow start in IPL 2024, Rahul finished as the franchise's leading run-scorer, amassing 539 runs that season and 593 in IPL 2025."We backed KL Rahul and gave him a particular role. From the first season to the second, we worked on building his confidence. We told him he would have our support, and that was important. He delivered. He told us that if we backed him, he would deliver the results, and he did," he says.Rao also stressed that backing the coaching staff and management is central to building a successful franchise. Citing Chennai Super Kings' turnaround after a difficult 2020 season and RCB's consistency in reaching the playoffs before winning the title in 2025, he said teams needed to trust their cricketing personnel and allow them to work."The difference between teams that win championships and those that don't is often the support staff, the processes and the freedom given to people. Miracles may happen occasionally, but consistency is what helps teams win trophies and matches. Look at teams like CSK, Mumbai Indians and Kolkata Knight Riders. When the management gives people a free hand, it makes a difference."I still remember Chennai Super Kings having a difficult season in 2020. They didn't finish in the top four, but from what I heard from MS Dhoni, he maintained the same atmosphere in the dressing room and didn't allow outside interference. The following season, they won the trophy."You can see something similar with Royal Challengers Bengaluru (RCB). The hard work over three years helped them consistently qualify for the playoffs. When I spoke to Faf du Plessis, who was with us at DC, he told me that the cricketing decisions were largely left to the cricketers. The management was involved, but the cricketing people had the freedom to do their job."In franchise cricket, you often see the difference when the people responsible for cricket are allowed to take decisions. There is a lot of noise on social media, with people asking teams to change this or that. But if you keep interfering, the franchise will always struggle to build consistency," he adds.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Why Mohammed Siraj's absence from Wellington Test is harsh but not a surprise
articles.summary: WELLINGTON: Mohammed Siraj was the most trending keyword as India stepped onto the field for the first Test against New Zealand.
articles.body: WELLINGTON: Mohammed Siraj was the most trending keyword as India stepped onto the field for the first Test against New Zealand. His omission from the series opener triggered a massive debate. While it's harsh on the proven match-winner, it doesn't come as a surprise. The sequence of events, starting with the one-off Test against Afghanistan, dropped enough cues about the team management's thinking.Siraj was asked to play the game with little turnaround time following the IPL 2026 final his team, Gujarat Titans (GT), played. He wasn't considered for ODI cricket, which followed, with Shubman Gill making it clear that the team prefers tall fast bowlers who can operate at pace. With no game time under his belt, Siraj boarded the flight to Sri Lanka for the two-Test series, and insufficient bowling volume was reflected in his rhythm during the Galle Test.His pace and penetration dropped drastically, leading to discussions about playing Gurnoor Brar for the Colombo Test. A late change of heart kept the experienced bowler in the playing XI for the second Test, but his returns were again underwhelming as Sri Lanka denied India a much-needed win. This takes nothing away from his ability to win matches for the country, but it forced the management to start exploring options.When the selectors, coach and captain discussed the bowling group for the New Zealand Tests, Siraj remained in the mix, but there was renewed excitement around Akash Deep regaining fitness. The likes of Anshul Kamboj and Auqib Nabi also joined the discussion because of their batting abilities. Siraj, meanwhile, was building his red-ball volume with outings in the Duleep Trophy and Ranji Trophy.The selectors dropped the next cue when they made him play just one India A game in New Zealand, keeping him with the ODI squad while the other Test bowlers, Akash Deep and Anshul Kamboj, were released for red-ball preparations. Siraj remained on the bench even in ODIs as late entrant Auqib Nabi, who replaced Prasidh Krishna in the squad, played ahead of him. It was only after Gurnoor Brar was added to the Test squad and released before the fifth ODI that Siraj played only his fifth ODI of the year.Before the first Test, Gill reiterated that they were looking at batting contributions from their bowlers at No. 8 and No. 9 and emphasised his preference for tall fast bowlers. The message was clear: they need bowlers with high pace to keep them in play during different phases of the Test.When asked about Siraj's exclusion, batting coach Sitanshu Kotak asserted that they played the XI the management felt best suited for these conditions. Kotak further added that Siraj remains world-class and said there was nothing wrong with the bowler that led to his omission from the Wellington Test.“There is nothing wrong. I mean, I can't see anything wrong,” Kotak told reporters after the day's play. “That's the best possible XI the team management thought, and that is the one which played. Sri Lanka, obviously, it was different conditions, and Siraj played both the Tests there.”Whether it's the right or wrong call is not the discussion right now; the focus should be on why the management's actions over the last few months and the build-up to this Test made his exclusion unsurprising.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: 'We want to get as many runs as possible': Nicholls eyes more frustration for India after stunning recovery
articles.summary: New Zealand turned the opening day of the first Test against India on its head with a remarkable fightback led by Henry Nicholls and Glenn Phillips, who
articles.body: New Zealand turned the opening day of the first Test against India on its head with a remarkable fightback led by Henry Nicholls and Glenn Phillips, who rescued the hosts from a precarious position to put them in the driver's seat at the Basin Reserve in Wellington on Thursday. After India reduced New Zealand to 70/5, the duo combined resilience with counterattacking strokeplay to take the hosts to 243/5 at stumps, leaving the visitors with plenty of work to do on Day 2.Nicholls, who brought up a magnificent century, remained unbeaten on 113 off 221 deliveries, while Phillips was closing in on his hundred at 94 not out. The pair stitched together an unbeaten 173-run stand for the sixth wicket, completely shifting the momentum in New Zealand's favour.Speaking after the conclusion of Day 1, Nicholls stressed the importance of carrying the momentum into the second morning, insisting that the partnership must be extended and the first-innings total pushed as high as possible.Nicholls eyes bigger total, warns of India's fresh bowling attackReflecting on the team's recovery, Nicholls expressed satisfaction at reaching stumps without losing another wicket but acknowledged that the challenge was far from over. He emphasised the need to remain focused, particularly with India's bowlers expected to return with renewed energy on Day 2.“We want to get as many runs as possible. Considering where we were earlier and where we are now, it's pleasing that Glenn and I have managed to remain unbeaten overnight. However, we know we have to put in the hard work again tomorrow. The Indian bowlers will come back fresh in the morning, and our priority will be to build on this partnership and take the total as high as possible," Nicholls told reporters after Day 1.Nicholls praises Phillips' counterattacking approachThe left-handed batter also reserved special praise for his batting partner, highlighting Phillips' aggressive approach and ability to keep the Indian bowlers under pressure.“Glenn is great to bat with. The way he counterattacks and runs between the wickets puts tremendous pressure on the bowlers. We complement each other well because we are both very busy at the crease. When you have someone at the other end who is constantly looking to put the bowlers under pressure, it makes your job a little easier."He's also quite entertaining, as you might have heard on the stump mic, with some of his reactions to deliveries. He's a valuable part of our batting line-up, and his approach is quite different, as we saw from the very beginning today," he added.Nicholls, Phillips frustrate India with unbeaten 173-run standThe fifth-wicket breakthrough had initially put India in complete control, with New Zealand struggling at 70/5. However, Nicholls displayed tremendous patience and discipline to anchor the innings, remaining unbeaten on 113 off 221 balls, including 14 boundaries.Phillips, meanwhile, brought a different dimension to the partnership. The right-hander remained unbeaten on 94 off 182 deliveries, striking 13 boundaries and ensuring that the Indian bowlers could not settle into a rhythm.Their 173-run unbroken partnership off 322 deliveries not only prevented a potential collapse but also transformed what had been India's dominant day into a promising one for the hosts.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates.
